title: Illinois's 15th Congressional District Election, 2026
description: The 2026 general election for Illinois's 15th Congressional District pits three-term Republican incumbent Mary Miller against Democratic challenger Jennifer Todd. The district spans central and southeastern Illinois across 35 counties, from the Mississippi River to the Indiana border, and is heavily Republican-leaning with a Cook Partisan Voting Index of R+20. Miller, a member of the House Freedom Caucus, easily won the March 17 Republican primary with 73.6% of the vote, while Todd, a registered nurse and first-time candidate, won the Democratic primary with 45.8% in a four-way race. Key issues include rural healthcare access, Community Project Funding (earmarks), infrastructure investment, and the contrasting policy visions of a far-right incumbent versus a progressive challenger focused on working-class issues.
polling_note: No public opinion polls specific to the IL-15 general election race were found. The district is rated 'Solid R' by the Cook Political Report and similar outlets, reflecting its strong Republican lean.

candidates.name: Mary Miller
candidates.summary: Mary Miller is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Illinois's 15th Congressional District, first elected in 2020. A farmer and former business manager, she is a member of the House Freedom Caucus and serves on the Agriculture, Education and Workforce, and House Administration committees. Miller has been described as a far-right conservative and strong supporter of Donald Trump, winning her 2026 primary with 73.6% of the vote against two Republican challengers.

candidates.name: Jennifer Todd
candidates.summary: Jennifer Todd is a registered nurse and first-time candidate for public office who won the Democratic nomination for Illinois's 15th Congressional District in March 2026. A second-generation nurse, single mother, and daughter of a veteran, she holds nursing degrees from Kaskaskia College and Southern Illinois University and has worked in ICU, hospice, school nursing, and healthcare insurance appeals. Todd campaigned on expanding healthcare access, protecting Medicare and Medicaid, securing Community Project Funding for the district, and supporting public education and family farms.

forecast.rationale: No public opinion polls exist for the IL-15 general election, so the forecast relies entirely on structural factors. The district has a Cook PVI of R+20 and is consistently rated 'Solid R' by nonpartisan election forecasters. Three-term Republican incumbent Mary Miller won her 2026 primary decisively with 73.6% of the vote, while Democratic challenger Jennifer Todd, a first-time candidate, won a four-way primary with only 45.8%. In a district this heavily Republican, with a strong incumbency advantage and no polling suggesting any shift, the Republican hold is overwhelmingly likely. Confidence is medium due to the absence of any general-election polling.
